messages:
Sam: Heads up 1: noticed p95 regressions on reranker/embeds routes after kernel-selector changes (favor fused kernels for short seqs). Dumping profiler snippets and an initial hypothesis + mitigation plan.

Maria: ok please paste traces and qps numbers

Sam: quick summary:
- embeddings (non-chat, short tokens) p50 roughly same, p95 up ~30ms
- reranker (many short candidates, <64 tokens) p95 up ~50-60ms, p99 worse
- kernel_switch rate jumped ~8x

Sam: profiler excerpt: 
```
route: reranker-v2
qps: 410
p50: 11ms
p95: 78ms (baseline ~13ms)
p99: 215ms (baseline ~110ms)
kernel_mix: fused_attn 46%, generic_fallback 54%
kernel_switches: 0.65/s -> 5.2/s after selector-v3
```

Jing: Does the batcher mix lengths? Continuous-batcher could be forming heterogeneous batches causing mid-batch kernel changes.

Sam: Exactly. Kernel-selector now picks fused for seq <=128. Batcher often mixes 8-16 token embeddings with 64-128 token rerank candidates, so kernel switches mid-batch and we pay context switch overhead. Also token_budget_target was lowered recently which increased batch churn.

Tyler: What are current batcher params for the two routes?

Sam: embeddings (non-chat) current: 
```
max_batch_size: 256
token_budget_target: 2048
max_wait_ms: 12
priority: fifo
```
Reranker used to have token_budget_target=4096 but someone reduced it to 2048 in a config flip.

Maria: Rough mitigation ideas:
- prefer length-homogeneous batching (seq buckets) for reranker
- sticky kernel selection per-worker with short TTL to avoid thrash
- adaptive token_budget for embeddings to avoid waiting too long but pack bursts
- bypass KV allocations in reranker path if we don't reuse KV between candidates

Jing: I ran a sim: grouping by floor(seq_len/32) into 4 buckets (0-31,32-63,64-127,128+) dropped kernel_switches ~75% in the sim and preserved packing for rerank workloads. For embeddings, buckets help less because arrivals are tiny and SLO tight.

Sam: Also found a small inefficiency: reranker code was allocating KV buffers per-candidate even though reranker is full-forward per candidate; skipping that allocation reduced memory churn in local tests. I'll push a small patch behind a feature flag.

Tyler: Concrete canary plan proposal:
1) Reranker: enable seq-length buckets (4 buckets as Jing suggested), token_budget_target=8192, max_wait_ms=20, keep max_batch_size conservative.
2) Embeddings (non-chat): adaptive glidepath: start token_budget=1024 & max_wait_ms=8, escalate to token_budget=4096 & max_wait_ms=25 if queue_depth > 48 for >10ms.
3) Kernel-selector: add per-worker sticky kernel TTL=5s (avoid mid-batch changes).
4) Deploy reranker KV-allocation bypass on canary workers.

Maria: I like 1,3,4. For 2 be careful 1: longer waits can harm p50. Adaptive escalation seems the right compromise.

Jing: I'll draft a PR that adds seq-buckets config and an adaptive token_budget state machine for routes. I'll include a micro-simulator in tests (Poisson arrival, real-world seq distribution) to assert kernel_switches, p95 and token packing efficiency.

Sam: Also we recently rolled a quantized-fallback weights build which bumped generic kernel usage; that made overall selector sensitivity worse. I'd prefer we revert global selector-v3 until canaries validate.

Tyler: Perf gating: require canary p95 <= baseline + 10ms and kernel_switches/s <= 1.5x baseline before promotion. Canary rollout: us-west-2, 5% traffic, 24h window. Collect token-packing and cost delta.

infra-bot: deploy: reranker-length-buckets canary started us-west-2 at 2025-11-05T16:05:12Z

Sam (later): After turning on seq-buckets + sticky TTL on canary: reranker p95 ~15ms, kernel_switches ~0.95/s, token packing slightly improved. Embeddings adaptive glidepath still testing but initial runs show ~15-25% packing improvement without p50 regression when thresholds tuned.

Maria: Great. Action items: revert global selector-v3, canary reranker changes (buckets+TTL+KV-bypass), canary embeddings adaptive glidepath, add perf-gate to canary job, 24h canary with cost telemetry.

Sam: I'll attach flame traces and KV alloc traces to the PR.

Jing: PR incoming. I'll add the simulation harness and a metric checker for kernel_switch rate.

Tyler: I'll own the canary rollout plan and perf gating config in infra CI.

Maria: Thanks team :thumbsup: Keep kernel-selector behind feature flag until we validate across load shapes.
